articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Imposes New Cuba Sanctions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, alongside significant new sanctions against Cuba.

As part of this action, OFAC published a Cuba-related Determination pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order 14404, specifically targeting the 'Electronics, Manufacturing, Marine, and Technology Sectors of the Cuban Economy.' This determination broadens the scope of industries where activities can lead to sanctions under E.O. 14404.

Additionally, OFAC made changes to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, including the addition of two Cuban-flagged vessels, EMILIA and GLORIA C, linked to Cuban state-owned enterprises. The action also included designations against entities associated with the Cuban regime's oil shipping networks and China-based suppliers of its military forces.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at disrupting Iran's illicit financial networks. OFAC also published an alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' highlighting the risks of providing services to vessels using deceptive practices to circumvent U.S. sanctions.

The alert emphasizes that Iranian shadow fleet operators increasingly use fraudulent registries or falsely claim flags without supporting documentation to create a veneer of legitimacy for illicit activities. OFAC warns of substantial risks of designation or penalties for those providing services to such vessels.

In addition, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, 'Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or After December 18, 2026,' and an amended Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 595). This general license further delays the effectiveness of the authorization in GL 5.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License for Wind-Down of Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.'

This amended general license provides authorization for transactions that are ordinarily incident and necessary to wind down operations with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.
The issuance of this general license follows previous Iran-related designations and aims to facilitate an orderly cessation of activities with the specified entity.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Bank Data Insights

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Under North Korea and DRC Sanctions Programs
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under its North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) sanctions programs.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting the North Korean regime and address human rights abuses and corruption in the DRC.
Specific details regarding the newly designated individuals and entities have been added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, for $1,529,685.

The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to a Russian defense manufacturer, Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA).

MMZA was deemed a blocked person by operation of law due to its majority ownership by designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, a Russian state-owned defense company. OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed, and the settlement amount reflects these findings.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting Requirements
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review to ensure published guidance remains current.

The updated FAQs, specifically numbers 10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, address topics related to blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC. These revisions clarify when financial institutions must freeze funds versus rejecting prohibited transactions, and update reporting procedures.

Key changes include updated filing instructions for initial blocking and rejected-transaction reports through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS), expanded descriptions of supporting documentation, and explicit annual report requirements for blocked property. The amendments also reinforce the distinction between an inquiry and a payment instruction, clarifying reporting obligations.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / KPMG Trade & Customs

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Entities, and Amends GLs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain entities and individuals from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under the Belarus and North Korea sanctions programs.

Under its North Korea sanctions program, OFAC delisted Chinese national Lu Hezheng and two Chinese entities, Shanghai Moxing Cultural Media Co. Ltd. and Shanghai Hongman Cartoon and Animation Design Studio, which had been sanctioned in 2021 for ties to a North Korean government-run animation studio. Belarusian national Andrei Alekseevich Rybakov was also delisted from the Belarus sanctions program.
Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended several Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these sanctions programs.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Export Compliance Daily

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Chinese Entities Under PAIPA for Intellectual Property Theft, Issues General Licenses
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA), targeting Chinese entities involved in the theft of trade secrets from U.S. persons.

The designations include Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co Ltd (Zhisuan), Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd (MiraclePlus), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (Phase I), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (Phase II), and Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Zhiyuan Enterprise Management Center Limited Partnership (Zhiyuan Enterprise). These entities are linked to a scheme to replicate Google's super intelligence (SI) infrastructure technology.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, 'Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations,' and PAIPA General License 2, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026.' General License 2 provides a time-limited authorization for winding down transactions until January 19, 2027.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief Efforts
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License 60A, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela.'
This amended general license aims to facilitate humanitarian aid and recovery efforts following recent earthquake activity in Venezuela.
In addition to the general license, OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarification on authorized transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Cuba Entity, and Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation, alongside the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.

The Iran-related designations targeted 16 individuals and 10 entities, including financial institutions like International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company, and Jazireh International Bank Company, for their role in supporting the Iranian regime's financial activities. These actions are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' to disrupt Iran's financial networks.

Additionally, OFAC designated Cuba's BANCO INTERNACIONAL DE COMERCIO S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to E.O. 14404. OFAC also issued Iran-related General License FF, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance,' and new and amended Cuba-related and Russia-related FAQs and General Licenses.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.
